checks.note: getMessages and getConversationForSse gate only via verifyIsParty, whose PLAYER arm passes when the caller's profile id equals conv.getPlayerId() — no AgeMessagingPolicy/visibleToPlayer check, unlike getConversations (visibleToPlayer filter) and sendMessage (playerIsBlocked throw). The caveat is satisfied in-file: initiateConversation's comment and the playerIsBlocked guards show blocked-tier ROLE_PLAYER callers are expected, and updateLastRead's PLAYER case does advance playerLastReadAt.

softDeleteMessage only rejects UNDER_REVIEW/BLOCKED and already-deleted messages, so a sender can delete an APPROVED message; it sets deletedAt and saves with no event or emitter call. getMessagesForPlayerConversation (oversight) reads via findByConversationIdAndNotDeleted, so the deleted message disappears from the parent's view silently.

MessagingReportService.reportMessage confirms the trigger: verifyIsParty allows the sender, the only guard is the duplicate-report check (existsByMessageIdAndReportedBy), and the status block unconditionally flips any non-BLOCKED message to UNDER_REVIEW. But the claimed consequence — content hidden from the recipient and parent — depends on toMessageDto nulling UNDER_REVIEW content for all viewers, which is in code not shown here.

getMessages and sendMessage both do conversationRepository.findById(...).orElseThrow(ResourceNotFoundException) before verifyIsParty (OperationNotAllowedException → 403 per the in-file comment), so missing vs foreign ids are distinguishable; the sibling getMessagesForPlayerConversation deliberately normalizes to 403 ("always 403, never 404"), confirming these two paths lack that guard.

matches.note: R1 identifies the same sanitizer weakness at the same place, covering plain-format phone bypass plus the obfuscation bypasses (at/dot emails, spelled-out and non-ASCII digits) with the same consequence of contact details passing unredacted.

R2 states the sanitizer is never applied to messages and Gemini is the sole control, a fragment of F2, but never raises the persist-before-moderation send path or the missing supervised-conversation handling as a defect.

R2 and R9 jointly describe the single-pass non-recursive replace allowing delimiter reconstruction and prompt injection in both GeminiModerationService and ReviewModerationService, same mechanism and consequence.
R6 covers the unthrottled message sending with Gemini cost amplification and R7 covers the sanitize-preview bypass oracle, together covering both halves of F4.
No reported finding mentions suspended coaches or locked users retaining messaging access.
No reported finding mentions the missing @Version/full-row save race that overwrites a concurrently committed BLOCKED status.
